Ref: EXAMPLE - delete on first real entry. THE APPEND-ONLY ATTESTATION LEDGER (SN-029). One row per accepted attestation: which artifact; a digest of the NORMATIVE TEXT that was accepted; the reviewed commit that accepted it; and the decision. Rows are APPENDED and never rewritten - the whole point is that the anchor cannot move under the thing it anchors. Decision vocabulary: ratified (a first acceptance) | clarity (an amendment an adjudicator judged wording-only, so the attestation carries over) | meaning (an amendment that moved the obligation - the row records the judgement; the artifact owes a fresh ratification) | override (a human overruling an adjudicator's verdict). WHY A LEDGER AND NOT GIT ARCHAEOLOGY: the baseline used to be DERIVED by walking the registry's history for the newest commit where a row still read Verified. That is only sound while every amendment flips its row's Status in the same commit - and the SANCTIONED amend+flip path is exactly the one the staged-amendment guard deliberately ignores, so a derived baseline can point at a commit whose text already contains an unratified change. A digest recorded at acceptance time catches that regardless of any Status movement. It also gives SN prose an anchor it structurally lacks: an SN has no Status cell at all.
